Howard T. Cash (born December 20, 1953) is an American photographer known for his documentary and fine art work focusing on Africa and the African diaspora. His work explores themes of cultural identity, history, and community.
Early life and education
Cash was born in Harlem, New York, and raised in Manhattan and the Bronx. He attended Holy Name Catholic School and later studied at Laurinburg Institute and Furman University. He completed his studies at Los Angeles City College, earning an Associate in Arts degree and a certificate in color photography.
Career
Cash began his photography career in the 1970s while attending Los Angeles City College, where he worked as a staff photographer for The Collegian.
In 1978, he participated in Operation Crossroads Africa, traveling to Ghana, which influenced his focus on African and diasporic subjects.
From 1979 to 1984, Cash lived and worked in Nigeria as a freelance photographer. He contributed to publications including The Guardian (Nigeria) and worked as a stringer for the Associated Press.
During this period, he photographed cultural and political subjects, including Afrobeat musician Fela Anikulapo-Kuti.
Following his return to the United States, Cash continued producing work focused on African-American communities and the broader African diaspora.
Exhibitions and recognition
Cash’s work has been exhibited in galleries and institutions including the Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture and Strivers’ Row Gallery in Harlem.
He has been recognized by the Bronx Council on the Arts, receiving a Bronx Recognizes Its Own (BRIO) award.
Publications and media
Cash’s work has been featured in publications and organizations including Amsterdam News, Harlem World Magazine, and En Foco.
